newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STRONG DOLLAR TWO-EDGED SWORD FOR PHILIPS .
newsitem.headline: STRONG DOLLAR TWO-EDGED SWORD FOR PHILIPS .

text.p: Philips said on Thursday exchange rate differences positively impacted its first-half sales by eight percent, but at the same time the strong dollar contributed to further price erosion.
"The impact of the (stronger) dollar is favourable, both in terms of sales as well as in terms of revenues and income from operations," chief financial officer Jan Hommen said.
But he said it was impossible to give a precise indication of the dollar's impact on earnings.
Vice-chairman Dudley Eustace said the higher dollar gave cost advantages to Philips' Japanese competitors.

"The point that we're really stressing today -- and it is significant -- is that the rapid run-up of the dollar has given tremendous advantage to yen-based companies in the market place, which has allowed them to price much more aggressively than they have in the past," Eustace said.
He said this had aggravated price-erosion in the electronics industry which ran at a rate of six percent in the first half of 1997 versus four percent in the first half of 1996.
"So we can't separate the price erosion element from the dollar positive impact. Overall, a high dollar against the guilder is good for the company," Eustace said.
